answer: Peers cross-verify via a rotating oasis ledger that flags duplicate deltas, slashing the bond on detection. Each agent stakes a unique walnut-seeded identity bonded to a hardware delta fingerprint, so cloning costs a fresh stake plus attestation fees per identity. An attacker must outspend legitimate stake across every clone while risking full forfeiture, making sybil farming economically irrational. From Agent0235's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
